The analyzed JET hybrid discharge #94875 had a toroidal magnetic field of 2.8 T, plasma current of 2.2 MA, 27 MW of neutral beam injection power, and 6.1 MW of ion cyclotron resonance heating power.
The authors considered two versions of impurity profiles - a nominal case and a case with 15% reduced Z_eff, to investigate the sensitivity of ETG turbulence predictions to impurity content.

QuaLiKiz 2.8.2 included improvements to the trapped electron mode (TEM) dependence on collisionality and a recalibration of the ETG saturation rule, reducing the ETG saturation level by a factor of 1/3 compared to 2.6.1.

With QuaLiKiz 2.6.1, the inclusion of ETG turbulence led to an anti-GyroBohm isotope scaling prediction, where increasing the main ion mass improved confinement. This effect was significantly reduced in the newer QuaLiKiz 2.8.2 version.

The improved ion heat confinement in the hybrid scenario was attributed to increased E×B rotation shear and electromagnetic (EM) stabilization of ion temperature gradient (ITG) turbulence, leading to higher T_i/T_e ratios.
The multiscale GENE simulations did not produce significant ETG heat flux, contradicting the rules-of-thumb used in QuaLiKiz 2.6.1 to predict the onset of ETG turbulence.

The improved trapped electron mode (TEM) modeling and recalibrated ETG saturation rule in QuaLiKiz 2.8.2 reduced the predicted importance of ETG turbulence and the associated anti-GyroBohm isotope scaling compared to the 2.6.1 version.

The authors noted that the ad-hoc nature of the electromagnetic (EM) stabilization model in QuaLiKiz is a caveat, and that the model's inability to capture ballooning modes and non-local effects in the inner core region is a limitation.
The time window analyzed for discharge #94875 was 8.25-8.55 seconds, at the beginning of the stationary-state flattop following the density buildup after the L-H transition.
The kinetic profiles, source and equilibrium data, and impurity profiles were averaged within the 8.25-8.55 second time window for the analysis.
The initial q-profile applied within the integrated modeling was calculated by EFIT++, and the kinetic profile fits were carried out with Gaussian Process Regression using EX2GK.
The NBI and ICRH deposition profiles were calculated by TRANSP using NUBEAM and TORIC, respectively.
The impurity profiles for Be, Ni, and W were inferred by a method incorporating multiple diagnostics for constrained consistency.
The measured radiation characteristics (total P_rad = 9.2 MW) were kept constant through simultaneous modification of Ni and W impurity profiles.
The JINTRAC-QuaLiKiz integrated modeling reproduced the experimental measurements of T_i, T_e, and n_e within the 1σ error envelopes for the base-case simulations.
